finding.title: Wire the profileId-in-PK schema-check invariant into the CI-invoked Makefile

evidence.quote: ci: analyze validate-calendar test ## Run full CI pipeline (analyze + seed validation + all tests)

finding.why: tool/schema_check.dart (DNI-327) enforces the profileId-in-PK invariant that prevents a multi-profile data leak on shared devices — the digest's own rules table marks this rule [E]nforced. But it is wired ONLY into the root Makefile's `ci`/`schema-check` targets. CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) only ever runs `make ci`/`make audit` with `working-directory: learning_tracker`, which resolves to learning_tracker/Makefile's `ci: analyze validate-calendar test` — a target with no schema-check step and no learning_tracker/tool/schema_check.dart to call even if it wanted to. No doc (CONTRIBUTING.md, learning_tracker/README.md, learning_tracker/CLAUDE.md) tells a contributor to run the root Makefile. Net effect: a new Drift user-data table that omits profileId from its composite key today would pass CI cleanly, and would only be caught if someone manually ran `make schema-check` from the repo root — something nothing in the documented workflow ever asks for.
finding.recommendation: Move tool/schema_check.dart's invocation (or a copy of it) into learning_tracker/Makefile's `ci`/`audit` target and add a dedicated CI step/job that runs it, matching how test-rules/arb-parity are wired. Retire the root Makefile's copy once the inner one is authoritative.
acceptance_criteria: learning_tracker/Makefile's `ci` or `audit` target invokes the profileId-in-PK schema checker and fails the build on a violation.
.github/workflows/ci.yml has a step/job that runs the schema checker on every PR.
A regression test (e.g. a table intentionally missing profileId in a fixture) proves the checker fires and the CI step goes red.
